# #536 — Capture spool-on-outage must be LOUD: report the failure visibly in-session while the session keeps working

## Operator ruling (Rico, 2026-08-03, during the #522 canon review)

On the fail-open split (caller errors loud / environment errors quiet): **"Both are fail."** Clarified to: when Open Brain is unreachable, the session KEEPS WORKING but the failure is visibly reported — no silent spooling. The two error kinds differ only in whether the session survives, never in whether anyone hears about it.

## Today's behavior (the delta)

Caller errors already fail loud with named reasons (#413/#431 family, sharpened by PR #532). Environment errors (server down, timeout) spool quietly by design — the operator learns about an outage only from the `spool N` count on the terminal gate line, and an agent mid-session learns nothing at all.

## Scope

- Stop/SubagentStop capture, checkpoint, and event writes: when a write lands in the spool because the server was unreachable, surface a visible one-line notice on the session's user-facing channel (hook systemMessage / stderr per surface) — e.g. "open-brain unreachable — turn spooled for replay (spool: N)". Content-free, bounded, once per event not per retry storm.
- The session must still never die from an OB outage — fail-open survival is unchanged; only the silence goes.
- Dedup/rate-bound the notice so a long outage doesn't spam every Stop.

## Acceptance

Live proof: kill the local service, produce a turn, observe the visible notice and the spool row; restart, replay, observe drain. Plus a test proving the notice fires on the unreachable path and does NOT fire on success.

This ruling amends the promoted canon rule derived from #431/#413 (fail-open split) — the canon text ships with the loud-spool wording, and this issue is the code catching up to it.

## Discussion (2)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-04T04:33:20Z

Closed by PR #542 (merged f705fc9) after three rounds: implementation, then two adversarial verify/fix cycles. Final state, all independently measured by a hostile verifier with its own probes:

- Outage notice fires once per outage with a 5-minute rate bound — 6 alternating fail/succeed Stops produce 2 lines (was 6); 80 flapping Stops produce 2 (was 80). Genuine outage: one degraded line, one recovery bookend carrying the held-turn count.
- The latch lives in its own sqlite file (`<watermark>.outage.sqlite`) so telemetry can never block delivery: healthy Stop under latch contention measured 0.29s with the turn delivered (was 31.3s with the turn DROPPED — a defect the PR itself had introduced and the verifier caught).
- `OPENBRAIN_SPOOL_PATH` is a declared setting; setting it no longer kills capture.
- Repeat failures inside a known outage demote from warning to debug — first one stays loud.

Live package reinstalled on this machine (`uv tool install --force ./python/openbrain`, 8 executables) — the next real Stop runs this code. The issue's kill-the-service live drill was deliberately left to the operator: say the word and I'll run it (brief dogfood outage, turns spool and replay by design). One residual: whether Claude Code surfaces hook stderr to the operator remains unverified from in-repo evidence — if a real outage produces no visible line, the surface choice needs revisiting (noted in the PR self-review).
